rules: Before dispatch, bind affected behavior and contract consumers to available test targets, existing regressions, required new cases and exact commands. Changed-file count alone does not establish impact.

Select the Cargo compile target before listing or filtering tests: --lib, --test <target>, --bin <target> or --doc as applicable. Bare cargo test -p, workspace/all-target/all-feature sweeps and unscoped --list are not ordinary defaults. Include compilation and linking in the cost estimate.

Use source and manifest inspection to identify targets before compiling. Bind package/target, test names or reviewed module filter, command flags, relevant source/dependency/fixture/schema/configuration bytes, toolchain/platform/environment, expected coverage and escalation reason. Verify that required selected tests actually execute and are not ignored; zero tests is not evidence.

Keep existing commands distinct from TO CREATE cases. A SELECT BEFORE DISPATCH recipe is an unresolved planning obligation, not an executable command, successful check or permission to invent a test name.

Preserve affected negative cases, invariants, consumer integration and applicable wire/codegen/reference proof. Broaden for demonstrated cross-cutting impact or insufficient narrower evidence; never broaden solely because a commit, workstream, push, worker or session finished.

Reuse compatible incremental build artifacts and CARGO_TARGET_DIR when useful. A warm build cache is not a passed test verdict; reuse test evidence only for matching checked subjects and covered claims.

The routine full product panel is reserved for NEXT-CLOSE.3. A concrete cross-cutting change with no sufficient narrower proof or an explicit owner request can justify another scoped full panel; workers report that need instead of automatically launching it.

After failure or interruption, retain successful stages only when their complete checked subjects still match. Run failed, invalidated and never-run required stages; unknown validity needs rechecking. Preserve any required order or shared-state continuity instead of splicing incompatible runs. Record every required stage/case and report combined evidence as an aggregate, never as one successful script invocation. A repaired step or unmeasured tail is not a passed panel.
Planning validation checks these obligations and packet shape only. It executes no verification binding, product gate or campaign task and does not change the execution hold.
workstream_acceptance: Review the actual workstream delta and affected contract consumers; bind and execute sufficient targeted integration checks, preserving applicable negative/invariant/wire/codegen proof. Reuse only matching-subject evidence. Workstream completion alone does not require the full product panel; record any concrete reason to broaden and the actual checked scope.
baseline_acceptance: Capture available baseline evidence and run only checks needed to establish the first authorized implementation frontier and its assumptions. Record measured, failed, unavailable and unmeasured areas explicitly; a full product panel is not a Phase 0 prerequisite unless concrete cross-cutting uncertainty cannot be resolved more narrowly.
final_acceptance: After scaffold removal, establish complete permanent final-product panel and decisive domain/ETO/HOME/Docker plus DP1-to-DP2 migration/documentation evidence for the accepted subject. Resume interrupted proof by checking failed, invalidated and never-run stages; reuse successful stages only with matching complete subjects. No unmeasured tail or unrelated green run counts as final acceptance.
